what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Peru in the United States: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 66521 Peruvian asylum seekers in the United States, 58.4% of all asylum seekers from Peru.
Refugees from Peru, a separate group, live mostly in the United States, Canada, Spain and Italy.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Peru with Sendero Luminoso from 1995 to 1999 and from 2007 to 2010, and an interstate armed conflict between Ecuador and Peru in 1995.
The fact pack records no armed conflict in Peru in recent years, so it does not say why the number of asylum seekers grew.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 1304 asylum seekers.
The figure reached its highest point, 69220, at the end of 2024, and the main years of displacement in the data are 2023 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the United States.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the United States only.
